long_biography.plain_text:
The business that became Quasar began in 1986, when Diez and conservationist Dolores Gangotena turned repeated journeys through Ecuador into a specialized travel venture. He handled operations while Gangotena managed sales and guest service. Their complementary roles helped the enterprise grow into an established luxury expedition operator across the Galapagos and Patagonia. Later Ecuadorian filings named him president and recorded direct shareholdings in related companies, confirming that he was more than a hired manager.

Today the enterprise is still privately held in Ecuador. The founders remain involved, though three successors lead important functions. The equity allocation across people and holding entities is not disclosed. Borrowed capital, operating assets, booking revenue and property values belong to those companies or family structures, not automatically to Diez himself. His identifiable fortune therefore stems from creating and retaining interests in a hospitality business. No dependable figure is available for his personal net worth.
